correction: STORY-02-005 used dq_rules/synthea_*.yml glob but per-table convention per LLD §5.1 and patient_360/CLAUDE.md is dq_rules/{table}.yml (no synthea_ prefix)
pattern: Always cite the project CLAUDE.md / LLD §5.1 file-naming convention before encoding glob patterns in AC Verification blocks; per-table SE rule YAMLs use {table}.yml not synthea_{table}.yml

correction: User re-adopted Unity Catalog OSS as the runtime catalog in LLD v1.13 (named side-catalog wiring + Liquibase-precreated EXTERNAL Delta), reversing the 2026-05-12 Derby/path-based revert; required flipping every story write-method/catalog wording back to UC insertInto/MERGE and adding spark-thrift-server + liquibase + make ddl-apply infra.
pattern: When a runtime-catalog decision is re-adopted/reversed, reconcile write-method wording in EVERY layer build story (not just the first-touched epics): read path (spark.read.table unity.<schema>.<table>), write path (insertInto/MERGE INTO unity.<schema>.<table>, never saveAsTable/path-based .save), the verification grep/forbidden_grep blocks, and any new deploy infra (pre-create DDL step) woven into bootstrap + integration-test + deploy-validation story ACs.

correction: Bronze/Silver-fact write ACs used insertInto with .option(replaceWhere) which is a bug — insertInto silently ignores replaceWhere, causing re-runs to append/double data. Corrected to mode(overwrite).insertInto with spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode=dynamic.
pattern: When a write AC pairs .insertInto() with .option(replaceWhere, ...), flag it as a bug: insertInto ignores replaceWhere. Idempotent per-partition writes MUST use mode(overwrite).insertInto with spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode=dynamic, and the Spark-session foundation AC must set that conf. replaceWhere only applies to .save()/.saveAsTable().

correction: v3.0 placed beeline-applied DDL under per-layer ddl/bronze/; LLD v1.24 actually specifies a single flat ddl/migrations/ dir of plain dated <YYYYMMDD>_<NNN>_<table>.sql files applied in lexical order by _infra/docker/ddl-apply.sh / make ddl-apply.
pattern: When a backlog cites a DDL/migration path, always read the LLD intro/§9.1/§13 file-naming convention first and use the exact directory + filename shape it prescribes (e.g. flat ddl/migrations/<YYYYMMDD>_<NNN>_<table>.sql applied in lexical order), never an assumed per-layer subdir like ddl/bronze/.
